protocol.py: 5 biology problems (5 notes).

1. NOTE NO-NEGATIVE-CONTROL: No blank on a dilution series: 6 wells of compound 1
   line 40:  p300.dispense(90, plate_dilution["A1"])
   At line 40 the robot starts a dilution series of compound 1 in NEST 96 Well Plate 200 µL
   Flat (slot 1): 6 wells at 6 concentrations, each level about 3 times weaker than the one
   before. No well on this plate holds dmso with no sample, so there is no blank: the curve
   has no zero to read against, and a signal from the diluent or the plastic cannot be told
   from the lowest point. Wells: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5 and A6 in slot 1.
   Affected: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5 and A6 in slot 1.
   Fix: Add a well of dmso alone, and tell the plate map where it is.
   Source: MIQE 2009: a no-template control on every plate is essential
           https://gene-quantification.com/miqe-bustin-et-al-clin-chem-2009.pdf
   Source: MIQE 2.0 (2025): the no-template and no-RT controls, still essential
           https://academic.oup.com/clinchem/article/71/6/634/8119148
   Source: Bustin 2025: MIQE compliance remains patchy
           https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC12154065/fullTextXML
   Source: Qiagen bench guide: PCR controls (no-template, no-RT, positive)
           https://www.qiagen.com/en-us/knowledge-and-support/knowledge-hub/bench-guide/pcr/reference-genes-and-controls/pcr-controls
   Source: Bio-Rad real-time PCR applications guide: controls in triplicate
           https://www.bio-rad.com/webroot/web/pdf/lsr/literature/Bulletin_5279.pdf
   Source: Thermo Maxima SYBR manual: the NTC contains all components except template DNA
           https://assets.fishersci.com/TFS-Assets/LSG/manuals/MAN0012933_Maxima_SYBR_Green_qPCR_Master_ROX_Sol__k0251_UG.pdf
   [3be7d243979b]

2. NOTE CONTAM-WELL: A used tip carried dmso (well A1 in slot 4) into well A1 in slot 1 it
was never meant for
   line 47:  p300.aspirate(30, plate_dilution["A1"])
   At line 47 the tip touched the liquid in well A1 in slot 1 while it still carried dmso
   (well A1 in slot 4) from an earlier step. A tip that has touched one liquid leaves a
   little of it in the next liquid it touches. The protocol never transfers that liquid into
   this well on purpose, so it was not meant to be there. If the wells hold different
   samples, each now holds a little of another. Liquid was later taken out of the affected
   wells, and the unwanted material went along into 1 other well: well A1 in slot 2.
   Affected: well A1 in slot 1.
   Also reached 1 other well: well A1 in slot 2.
   Fix: Use a fresh tip for each well at line 47. If one tip must serve many wells, dispense
   from above the liquid (for example `well.top()`) so that the tip never touches what is
   already in the well.
   Source: Lab Manager: minimizing cross-contamination in automated liquid handling
           https://www.labmanager.com/minimizing-cross-contamination-in-automated-liquid-handling-workflows-35194
   [bbcdc865aae4]

findings.title: No blank on a dilution series: 6 wells of compound 1
findings.explanation: At line 40 the robot starts a dilution series of compound 1 in NEST 96 Well Plate 200 µL Flat (slot 1): 6 wells at 6 concentrations, each level about 3 times weaker than the one before. No well on this plate holds dmso with no sample, so there is no blank: the curve has no zero to read against, and a signal from the diluent or the plastic cannot be told from the lowest point. Wells: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5 and A6 in slot 1.
findings.fix: Add a well of dmso alone, and tell the plate map where it is.

findings.title: A used tip carried dmso (well A1 in slot 4) into well A1 in slot 1 it was never meant for
findings.explanation: At line 47 the tip touched the liquid in well A1 in slot 1 while it still carried dmso (well A1 in slot 4) from an earlier step. A tip that has touched one liquid leaves a little of it in the next liquid it touches. The protocol never transfers that liquid into this well on purpose, so it was not meant to be there. If the wells hold different samples, each now holds a little of another. Liquid was later taken out of the affected wells, and the unwanted material went along into 1 other well: well A1 in slot 2.
findings.fix: Use a fresh tip for each well at line 47. If one tip must serve many wells, dispense from above the liquid (for example `well.top()`) so that the tip never touches what is already in the well.

findings.fix: Use a fresh tip for each well at line 143. If one tip must serve many wells, dispense from above the liquid (for example `well.top()`) so that the tip never touches what is already in the well.
